name: Admin Accounting Income CRUD
description: Superuser manages income records at /panel/accounting/incomes, a list that lands on the builtin "Solo esperados" tab (kind=expected + paymentStatus=pending) rather than on "Todas": create via modal with automatic 50/50 partner split (editable), a period field that defaults to today's exact date with a month-only toggle (shared PeriodDateField; edits always open in full-date mode showing the stored day — 01 is the month-only storage sentinel — with the toggle still downgrading to month), ledger selector (Contabilidad: Empresa / Personal Gustavo / Personal Carlos — personal hides the split and pocket destination and uses a single Valor field) which is a filter only, with no column of its own since Aug 2026, edit with prefill (PATCH /api/accounting/incomes/:id/update/), delete with ConfirmModal (DELETE .../delete/), HTML5 required validation and backend error toasts via usePanelNotify. The list opens ordered by Mes from newest to oldest; Mes toggles newest/oldest, while Total cycles highest/lowest/default Mes order. The active order survives filters, quick tabs, Agrupado/Clásico changes and later visits through browser storage. Expected rows carry a fulfilment state in their own "Cobro" column, computed from their linked liquid records (Pagado green tint / Parcial amber tint with the outstanding amount inline / Pendiente untinted). Expected company rows also expose an independent forecast level and manual inclusion switch across list, create/edit form and detail; changing the color preserves the switch, neutral means 'Sin clasificar', and duplication clears both. They retain two extra row actions: 'Liquidar', which opens a modal prefilled with the pending amount (destination defaults to Bolsillo ProjectApp; the payment period asks for the exact date by default, prefilled with today, with the 'Registrar el día exacto de pago' toggle downgrading to month-only) and POSTs to /api/accounting/incomes/:id/settle/, which registers the liquid record linked via expected_income (the expected row survives, so partial payments accumulate). Since Aug 2026 the amount received may be 0 when the shortfall is fully allocated: the settlement then creates no liquid record and sends no payment email — it only books the allocations (a deduction credits the parent as payment; a follow-up shrinks it), rescuing old partial collections whose fee-sized residual would otherwise stay 'Parcial' forever (the same path the resolve_income_residual management command uses). A fixed hint under the pending block tells the user that typing a lower received amount unlocks the resolution paths; when the amount received is below the pending balance the modal reveals the 'Saldo por resolver' section with the deductions group auto-expanded once per open (an untouched auto-added row — in either group — neither blocks the submit nor reaches the payload, so leaving the rest pending stays one click) with a live status badge next to the section total (info 'Sin asignar' while a remainder stays pending, success once the balance is fully resolved, danger with the excess when the allocation overflows) and two collapsible, repeatable groups: 'No es un cobro pendiente, es un gasto' (concept starts unselected behind a 'Seleccionar concepto' placeholder and must be picked explicitly — options Comisión plataforma de pago / Comisión bancaria / Retención en la fuente / Otro, the last one requiring free text; selector and amount share the row via a responsive grid that keeps the longest label readable and stacks below sm) which books the shortfall as an ExpenseRecord flagged with deduction_type and no pocket movement, and 'Sí lo voy a cobrar: crear ingreso esperado' which reschedules it as one or more new expected incomes inheriting the parent's ledger, destination and partner ratio. Both can be combined; follow-ups are subtracted from the expected record while deductions stay inside it as payment credit, so it closes with no orphan balance, and anything left unallocated simply stays pending as before. Each line amount input suggests the still-unassigned remainder as its placeholder and adopts it (selected, ready to overtype) on click or tab focus while empty; a zero remainder is suggested but never auto-filled. Every non-pristine line validates inline (red border + message under the row): missing concept, empty/zero amount, missing free text on Otro, missing concept/month on follow-ups, and the line whose amount pushed the sum over the balance is flagged with the excess without erasing what was typed. Over-allocating or any invalid line disables the submit and a persistent aria-live note next to the button explains why; an unallocated remainder never blocks. Deductions keep the expected income gross and count as payment credit via their source_income link; they reduce expected utility as real expenses (liquid utility already arrives net of them) and surface in the Gastos tab with a 'Descuento de ingreso' pill, a per-type filter and their own 'Naturaleza' filter, and 'Marcar como perdido', offered only on rows with no payments yet, which PATCHes kind=lost. Besides the landing tab the view ships two more builtin quick tabs: 'Hosting esperados' (the same cut plus the search term 'hosting', which seeds the search box) and 'Perdidos'; builtin tabs never drift, and '?accounting_incomeTab=all' opens the full list. Written-off income is a third kind, visible under 'Todos' and isolable via the builtin 'Perdidos' quick tab (or the 'Pérdidas' segment in the filter panel), with its own total chip and a 'Perdido (año)' KPI. Since Aug 2026 the row icons are a single three-dots button opening IncomeActionsModal (shared by the grouped and classic views, which had drifted apart), the Gustavo/Carlos columns moved into the income detail modal, and a Proyecto column joins Cliente. Since Aug 2026 every row also offers 'Duplicar' — available whatever the state, since the frequent case is reopening the next period of an already collected hosting — and the same action sits in the income detail modal. It does not write: it GETs /api/accounting/incomes/:id/duplicate-draft/ and opens the income form seeded with the original's concept, amounts, split, ledger, client, project, origin and notes, always as 'Esperado' and never carrying the original's settlement links, cuenta de cobro, deductions, history or silenced reminders. The proposed date is the original's plus one hosting cycle when the hosting behind it can be resolved unambiguously (labelled as such under the field); otherwise it opens empty and the field's required blocks the save until a date is chosen. Because most of the book carries no origin and no client, that lookup resolves for almost no income, so the form also offers cadence shortcuts ('+1 mes', '+3 meses', '+6 meses', '+1 año') built server-side from the original's date: picking one fills the field (in month granularity when the exact-day toggle is off) and marks itself pressed, and it overrides the hosting proposal when the two disagree. While the draft is being fetched the row's three-dots button spins and refuses a second click, since the action menu closes on click. Confirming POSTs through the ordinary create endpoint, so the new row gets a row flash and an 'Ingreso duplicado' toast that reads apart from a manual alta; a failing draft only raises 'No se pudo preparar el duplicado'. Since Aug 2026 an income with Origen Hosting swaps the single date for the period it covers, laid out in the order it is filled: Periodicidad rides in the top row beside Tipo (it is chosen before the dates it proposes), and inicio and fin share the row below so the range reads left to right, with the exact-day toggle under inicio — the date it applies to — and the cadence shortcuts under both. The Periodicidad catalog is the recurring-payments one and its hint says what it does for the user ('Al elegirla se calcula la fecha de fin del período'), not where the catalog came from. Picking a cadence recomputes immediately: it writes the inclusive end (start + cadence − 1 day, day clamped) and, when there is no start yet, opens the window on the period after the last one recorded — GET /api/accounting/incomes/period-suggestion/ resolves that antecedent by client, narrowed by project, and the start field states which period this one follows ('El período anterior terminó el …'); the first charge of a client falls back to today, and a client holding several active hostings with no project to tell them apart gets no proposal rather than a guessed one. Moving the start carries the end with it keeping the cadence, and writing the end by hand turns the cadence to 'Personalizada' instead of leaving the selector claiming a length the window no longer has; under 'Personalizada' both dates are written by hand and nothing recomputes. The recompute runs off the values themselves, so it also fires when the start is written programmatically — turning the origin to Hosting, or a shortcut. Switching the origin keeps everything already typed, but a create's untouched 'today' default is boilerplate rather than an answer and does not carry into the window, which is what lets the antecedent fill it. The cadence shortcuts ('+1 mes', '+3 meses', '+6 meses', '+1 año') are offered whenever a period is being OPENED — creating or duplicating, never while editing one already on the book — and each one anchors on the antecedent, so clicking several in a row re-lengthens the same window instead of walking a period further forward each time; the selector and the buttons stay in sync, with the pressed state reading back from both cadence and start. The three fields are required for hosting (creating and editing — legacy hosting rows complete their period on first edit), and fin must come after inicio, refused inline under the field before the submit as well as by the serializer. Other origins keep the single date, clearing any stray window, and their duplicate shortcuts still write the server-computed date. A duplicate always counts from the record it copies, never from today: the draft carries a period_anchor stating what it counted off, and the form anchors its own arithmetic on it. A recorded window proposes inicio = day after the recorded fin with the cadence's own length ('income_period'), and a legacy row falls back to the hosting-catalog lookup ('hosting_cycle'); both fix the inicio, so changing the periodicidad in the modal only moves the fin. When the original has neither -- no window and several active hostings to tell apart, which is the majority of the book -- the anchor is the original's own DATE ('original_date'): nothing is prefilled, because only the cadence can say how long that period lasted, and picking one opens the window where that period would have closed (fecha del original + periodicidad). That last anchor floats -- another cadence moves the whole window, since the fin it counts from is precisely what was never recorded -- while a start written by hand is never moved by a later cadence. A BaseAlert over the block says which of the three it was and names the dates, so a chained date is distinguishable from a guess; today is reached only when the original carries no date at all, and the notice says the range chains with nothing. The recorded window also rides into the cuenta de cobro as the pre-filled 'Período facturado', and the income export appends Período inicio / Período fin / Periodicidad columns. (Ago 2026) Origen is required on every income the form writes -- creating, editing and duplicating alike: BaseSegmented carries no native required, so the form refuses with 'Elige la linea de negocio del ingreso.' from the first submit attempt on, and the write serializer enforces the same on create and on any update that writes the field (a partial PATCH that does not touch it leaves a legacy row as unclassified as it was; settling is exempt, since the liquid child and the rescheduled balance copy the parent's line of business, blank included). Duplicating inherits origin like every other field that governs the shape of the form (origin, ledger, period_cadence; kind and destination are the declared overrides), so a hosting duplicate opens on the covered-window block and the other three lines on the single date. The copy is faithful rather than helpful: an original with no origin -- most of the book, which predates the field -- opens a duplicate with none, and a BaseAlert under the control says so ('El ingreso original no tiene origen registrado...') instead of letting a silent blank read as a copy that failed. The leading three-dots menu opens with Detalle e historial (the detail modal, which carries the record history) and Ver nota when the income has one; its kebab keeps the 44 px target.
